title: 'Once in a millennium' kept happening
hook: Your risk model says a crash this big happens once in thousands of years. Reality didn't read the model.

scenes.say: Your risk model says a crash this big happens once in thousands of years. Reality didn't read the model.
A black swan: rare, massive impact, and obvious only in hindsight.
Code simulates {days} days, about {years} years. One series is normal. One has fat tails, closer to real markets.
scenes.note: Simulation: normal vs Student-t (3 d.f.), same volatility

scenes.say: The normal model expects a five-sigma day about once every {normal_5s_expected_years} years.
The fat-tailed series had {fat_5s} of them.
Models built on the bell curve underestimate exactly the days that matter most.
Don't ask what's likely. Ask: if the unlikely happens, do I survive?

takeaway: Don't ask what's likely. Ask: if the unlikely happens, do I survive?
